role: Stage E sparse and noisy observation stress for the viscosity inverse on the Stage A harder Burgers pilot. This file is the scoring contract. It is not a test table.
question: How do the closed-form residual least squares and the Stage D operator-conditioned inverse degrade as observations get noisier and sparser, and where does each first exceed 10% mean relative error or first fail the 0.5 rule? A result where the operator advantage vanishes is an acceptable outcome.

hard_ood.name: hard_ood
hard_ood.complement: instances in the scored split with nu > threshold_nu

nu_search.grid: linspace(min, max, n_grid), both endpoints included

objective.name: stage_d_sensor_mse
objective.rule: Both Stage D arms selected lambda 0 on validation hard_ood. Stage E holds that choice fixed. It does not read the validation split and it does not add a new weight or a regularizer.

noise.distribution: i.i.d. standard normal on the saved grid, scaled by fraction times the population standard deviation of the clean field
noise.std_domain: all stored times and all spatial nodes of that instance's clean trajectory
noise.shared_epsilon: One epsilon field per (noise_seed, instance_id). Every mask and every positive fraction restricts or rescales that same field. Fraction 0 does not add it.
noise.extra_seed_role: Seeds 1 and 2 repeat only the closed-form noise axis, to show draw-to-draw movement of that estimator. They are not a second operator grid. Breakdown thresholds use the primary seed, which is the seed every method shares.

sensors.placement: equispaced periodic nodes starting at index 0, stride = n_space / n_sensors

operator_undefined.when: n_bursts == 1 leaves only the opening window, so the Stage D sensor objective has no target burst
operator_undefined.recorded_as: inapplicable, not as a 0.5-rule failure and not as a fabricated nu_hat

dense_ls_clean.role: No-noise ceiling. Every saved frame and every grid point of the clean field. Not recomputed under noise or under a sparse mask.

training_mean.role: Training-split mean viscosity. It does not read the test observations. The same slice values are the horizontal reference on every curve.

closed_form_ls.estimator: normal equation of the Stage 4 central Burgers residual on the condition mask

operator.estimator: Stage D sparse rollout sensor mean square, lambda 0, same 191-point grid

aggregation.operator_unit: one scalar per seed per slice
aggregation.threshold_uses: the across-seed mean, on primary noise seed 0

breakdown.rel_onset: first condition along the ordered axis whose mean relative error is greater than 0.1
breakdown.failure_onset: first condition along the ordered axis whose failure count is at least 1; for an operator arm the count is the across-seed mean, and the onset fires when that mean is greater than 0
breakdown.reference_already: if the reference cell already meets the predicate, the onset is that cell
breakdown.inapplicable_onset: first condition on the axis where the operator has no target burst

diagnostics_not_used_for_estimates: clean-field sensor u_xx alias at the condition's sensor count
sensor-curve identifiability (max - min) / min on the viscosity grid
counts of operator estimates sitting on the grid endpoints
not_claimed: a retuned hard_ood threshold, Stage 5 mask, or Stage A, B, C, or D protocol
a change to any previously reported number
that lambda was re-selected under noise or sparsity
a new regularizer, a learned inverse, or an architecture change
that noise seeds 1 and 2 were scored for the operator
that the one-burst mask has an operator estimate
that the dense least squares was shown noisy observations
that the noise standard deviation is computed from the sensors alone
that a vanishing operator advantage is a failure of the study
